title: Tariffs Raised Consumer Goods Prices, NY Fed Study Finds | Newstro Finance
summary: News summary of the New York Fed tariff study: about a quarter of a tariff reaches consumer goods prices within a year, a third of it via domestic goods, and slower inflation does not mean lower prices.

assertions.quote: tariffs added 2.9 percentage points to annual inflation in 67 categories of consumer goods by February 2026
the importer of record is responsible for applicable duties, taxes, and fees, even when using a broker
about 26% of a uniform tariff increase reaches average consumer goods prices after a year
Imported materials become costlier and reduced import competition can affect markups.
Slower inflation describes the pace of change. It does not automatically mean prices have returned to their earlier level.

verdicts.note: Inflation is the rate of change of the price level; a lower positive rate means prices rise more slowly, not that they fall.

assertions.quote: the tariff contribution to annual goods inflation fades, while the price level remains above their no tariff comparison
Those categories represent about 1/5 of the overall consumption basket, so this analysis cannot by itself explain every household bill.

verdicts.note: Services are about two thirds of the CPI basket and are largely untouched by tariffs, so goods-only estimates bound the tariff effect on headline inflation.

The 67 CPI items in the study cover 75 percent of non-oil consumer goods spending but only 20 percent of the overall consumption basket, and the authors say their relative-price estimates are not a forecast of aggregate CPI inflation.
The sample excludes services, about two-thirds of the consumer basket, and the comparisons across goods cannot establish how much of broader price movements was itself caused by tariffs.
